sentences.text:
1. Vide this Judgment, I intend to dispose off the suit for permanent and mandatory injunction filed by the plaintiff against the defendant no.1 and 2 who are his son and daughter-in-law respectively,
thereby seeking the relief that defendants be directed to remove themselves from the property bearing no. J- 281/9 Gali no.6 near Sibban Model Public School Teesra Pusta, New Usmanpur,
Delhi measuring 25 square yards (hereinafter as 'suit property') and to pay Rs 5000/- per month as occupation charges/mesne profits from the filing of the suit till the handing over the possession.
It is also prayed that defendants be restrained from creating third party in the above-mentioned property.
2. The plaintiff claimed himself to be owner of the suit property.
It is stated that defendants being the son and daughter- in-law of the plaintiff respectively were allowed to live on second floor of the suit property as a permissive user.

It is stated that conduct of the defendants towards the plaintiff is not good for which the defendants were disowned by the plaintiff from his movable/immovable properties vide publication in the newspaper dated 10.10.2020.
3.
It is stated by the plaintiff that he does not want to retain the defendants in the suit property and they were called to vacate the suit property vide legal notice dated 26.11.2020.
It stated that defendants not vacated the suit property and hence the present suit.

The defence of defendants was struck off vide order dated 12.07.2023 passed by Ld Predecessor of this court.
5. The plaintiff examined himself as PW1 and tendered his evidence by way of affidavit which is Ex.PW1/A.

In the judgment titled as N.G Dastane vs S. Dastane AIR 1975 SC 1534 it was held by Hon'ble Apex Court that the normal rule which governs civil proceedings is that a fact can be said to be established if it is proved by preponderance of probabilities and this is the reason that under section 3 of Indian Evidence Act, a fact is said to be proved when the court either believes it to exists or considers its existence so probable that a prudent man ought, under the circumstances of the particular case, to act upon the supposition that it exists.

The defendants have not set up any kind of documents qua the suit property in their defence.
In these circumstances, the case of the plaintiff is at better footing.

The legal notice dated 26.11.2020 Ex.PW1/8 and its proof of delivery Ex.PW1/9 reveals that defendants were asked to vacate the suit property by the plaintiff.

The testimony of PW1 is corroborated by the testimony of PW2 and PW3.
14.
When the defendant chosen not to contest the suit, their capacity in the property in question can be deduced to be of licensee only.
There is no document on record vide which the capacity of defendants in the suit property can be said to be of owner/tenants/mortgagee and so on.
15. The testimony of plaintiff went unchallenged.
The documents available on record specifically documents Ex.PW1/3 (colly) and Ex.PW1/8 creates a right in the favour of the plaintiff to get the suit property vacated from the defendants.
16. The defendants being the son and daughter-in-law of the plaintiff have no independent right in the suit property.
If their KAPIL by KAPIL KUMAR KUMAR Date: 2024.01.12 16:02:27 +0530 license has been terminated then they are liable to vacate the suit property.
17. By virtue of un-controverted testimony of the plaintiff and his witnesses, the plaintiff is able to discharge his burden of proof.
The defendants are under obligation to vacate the suit property.
18. Accordingly the suit of the plaintiff is hereby decreed.
The defendants are directed to vacate the area of the suit property which is under their possession and to hand over the same to the plaintiff.
The defendants are restrained from creating third party interest in the suit property.
19. The plaintiff has also prayed for mandatory injunction against the defendants thereby directing them to pay use and occupation charges/mesne profits at the rate of 5000/- per month.
The claim of the plaintiff as to the mesne profit at the rate of 5000/- per month remained unchallenged.
The mesne profits cannot be granted by virtue of mandatory injunction.

However considering the fact that defendants are in unauthorized occupation of the suit property when their license has already been terminated they are under obligation to pay mesne profits to the plaintiff.

20. It is necessary to first refer to Section 2(12) of the CPC, which defines mesne profits and also to Order XX Rule 12 CPC, which prescribes the procedure to be followed by the Court while dealing with a claim for grant of mesne profits.

These aforesaid provisions read as under:-
KAPIL by KAPIL KUMAR KUMAR Date: 2024.01.12 16:02:33 +0530 "Section 2(12)
"mesne profits" of property means those profits which the person in wrongful possession of such property actually received or might with ordinary diligence have received therefrom, together with interest on such profits, but shall not include profits due to improvements made by the person in wrongful possession;"
"Order XX Rule 12:-Decree for possession and mesne profits.-

21. The calculation of mesne profits always involves some guesswork and the Court can take take judicial notice of the prevalent market rents of different areas within the city while awarding mesne profits.

Rents may vary based on location of properties, nature of construction, a period of construction, purpose/ user for which the premises are let, variation between KAPIL KUMAR KUMAR Date:
2024.01.12 16:02:41 +0530 demand for tenanted premises and availability of premises and even factors relating to the position of the economy.

In this regard,
reference may be made to judgment of Suman Verma & Ors V. Sushil Mohini Gupta & Ors - 2014 (10) DRJ 595 wherein it was held that:-
"the calculation of mesne profits always involves some amount of guess work, as held by this court in International Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Saraswati Industrial Sundictes Ltd. (1992)
2 RCR 6, M.R. Sahni Vs. Doris Randhawa and reiterated in Consep India Pvt. Ltd.
supra and applicability of prevalent rents in the city and of which the Judges manning the Courts and who are born and brought up in the same city, are generally aware of."

sentences.text: What is now therefore to be determined is that what should be the mesne profits which should be awarded to the landlord in the absence of any evidence having been led by the landlord with respect to the rents prevalent in the area

If there is no registered lease deed for a fixed period of three years, then, the tenant continues to stay in the premises, not because of any relationship of landlord and tenant pursuant to a lease of three years but only as an unauthorized occupant after the KAPIL by KAPIL KUMAR KUMAR 16:02:47 Date: 2024.01.12 +0530 expiry of lease period by efflux of time.

I therefore do not agree with the argument of the learned counsel for the tenants and I hold that since in this case tenancy expired by efflux of time on 30.11.2000 and the suit was filed on 3.4.2001, clearly, the tenant would become liable to pay mesne profits from 1.12.2000.

Though it has not been argued on behalf of the landlord, I would like to give benefit to landlord of various precedents of this Court and the Supreme Court which take judicial notice of increase of rent in the urban areas by applying the provisions of Sections 114 and 57 of the Evidence Act, 1872.

In my opinion, considering that the premises are situated in one of the most centrally located commercial localities of Delhi, situated in Connaught Place, an increase of 15% every year should be awarded (and nothing has otherwise been shown to me for the increase to be lesser) during the period for which the tenants have over stayed in the tenanted premises.

Putting it differently, for the first year of illegal occupation,
the tenant will pay 15% increased rent over the contractual rent.
For the second year of illegal occupation, 15% increase will be over the original contractual rent plus the additional 15%.
It will be accordingly for all subsequent years of the illegal occupation till the premises were vacated on 3.4.2005.

I rely upon and refer to a Division Bench judgment of this Court in the case of S. Kumar v. G.R. Kathpalia 1999 RLR 114, and in which case the Division Bench has given benefit to the landlord and has taken judicial notice of increase in rent, and has accordingly allowed mesne profits at a rate higher than the contractual rate of rent."

We find that this Court has in several cases taken judicial notice of the factum of increase of rent CS No. 179/2020 Page No. 9 of 12 by KAPIL KAPIL KUMAR KUMAR Date:
2024.01.12 16:02:53 +0530 and made awards of mesne profits and damages.

Noteworthy in this behalf is a judicial pronouncement of the Division Bench reported at (supra) entitled Vinod Kumar v. Bakshi Sachdev.........
21
........It is true that no substantial evidence has been led by the plaintiff in respect of the increase of rent in the properties like that of the suit property.

However, it is a well known fact that the amount of rent for various properties in and around Delhi has been rising staggeringly and we cannot see why such judicial notice could not be taken of the fact about such increase of rents in the premises in and around Delhi which is a city of growing importance being the capital of the country which is a Zile Singh vs Pawan Kumar on 12 January, 2024

6 matter of public history.
At this stage we may appropriately refer to the Court making judicial notice of the increase of price of land rapidly in the urban areas in connection with the land acquisition matters.

Even the Apex Court has taken judicial notice of the fact of universal escalation of rent and even raised rent of disputed premises by taking such judicial notice in case of D.C. Oswal v. V.K.
Subbiah.

22. In that view of the matter we have no hesitation in our mind in holding that the Trial Court did not commit any illegality in taking judicial notice of the fact of increase of rents and determining the compensation in respect of the suit premises........"

24. A common vein of the judgment is that mesne profits, which a licensor is entitled to receive from a licensee who is continuously in the occupation of the licensed property despite the termination of the license, has been laid down to mean the rate of rent/license fees, which would otherwise, accrue on a suit premises during the period of its illegal occupation by a licensee.

However, the burden which the Courts are often tasked with is to determine the appropriate amount payable to the licensor towards KAPIL by KAPIL KUMAR KUMAR 16:03:04 Date: 2024.01.12 +0530 such mesne profits.
This process of determination of mesne profits begins with the licensor discharging the onus placed upon him to prove his claim for mesne profits, in accordance with the law.

Thereafter, it is for the Court to ascertain the appropriate mesne profits to be awarded to the claimant by adhering to the parameters as set out in Order XX Rule 12 CPC which prescribes that while passing the decree for possession, the Court may either straightaway pass a decree for mesne profits or direct that an inquiry be conducted for assessing the rate of mesne profits payable.

If the Court finds that it is sufficient and authentic evidence available on record for determination of the landlord's claim for mesne profits, the Court may, in its discretion, award the same by relying on such evidence.

In the alternative, in situations when the Court finds that the evidence brought on record is not sufficient for such determination, the court may direct that an inquiry be conducted thereto, in accordance with the provisions of the CPC and/or take judicial notice under Section 114 and 57 of the Evidence Act, 1872.
25.
Now coming to the case in hand qua the aspect of mesne profits.
The suit property is consisting of 25 square yards and the defendants are in the possession of one of the floor of the suit property consisting of one room, kitchen, toilet and bathroom.
The mesne profits at the rate of 5000/- per month is on higher side considering the area under the possession of defendants and the locality in which the suit property is situated.
The mesne- profits at the rate of 2500/- per month is fair and reasonable.
The plaintiffs are entitled to mesne profits at the rate of 2500/- per KAPIL by KAPIL KUMAR KUMAR
Date: 2024.01.12 16:03:09 +0530 month from the date of filing of the suit till the vacation of the suit property.
26. In view of the above-discussion the suit of the plaintiff is hereby decreed.

The defendants are hereby directed to remove themselves from the suit property i.e. property bearing no. J- 281/9 Gali no.6 near Sibban Model Public School, 3 rd Pusta, New Usmanpur, Delhi and to hand over the possession of suit property to the plaintiff.
The plaintiff is entitled to mesne profits at the rate of 2500/- per month from the date of filing of the suit till the vacation of the suit property.
Defendants are hereby restrained from creating third party interest in the suit property.
